guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
Journal With Each Hand

Write vulnerable thoughts and feelings with your non-dominant hand—the clumsy hand whose script already looks like a child wrote it. Answer with the dominant hand as the adult, offering love, protection, and guidance.

This can bypass the silence people hit with speech or visualization. If the protector is what appears, let that part use the non-dominant hand first. Don’t demand the child before the guard has spoken.
note: Turn 65 (2026-10-17): Simple Practices, practice 4 of 9 (Journal With Each Hand), for the dedup.
length: two paragraphs: the two-hand method, then PGQ-016
before: Picture the love traveling from your heart down to your little one. If they send a little back, great, pass it along down again and let it loop. If they don't, that's allowed (you already told them they don't have to love you back), and you just keep sending yours. No warmth today at all? Then rest your hands there and notice what you find, no faking required.
after: ## “And So That’s the Way It Happened!” (practice 5 of Simple Practices)
next: ## “And So That’s the Way It Happened!” (practice 5 of Simple Practices)
brief:
- the main point: journal with each hand: write vulnerable thoughts and feelings with the non-dominant hand, whose clumsy script already looks like a child's, and answer with the dominant hand as the adult offering love, protection and guidance; it can get past the silence people meet with speech or visualization; if the protector shows up, it gets the non-dominant hand first.
- what the dedup leaves to add (G4): the two-hand method; using it when speech or imagery meets silence; giving the protector that hand first.
- already in the article, so not said again: don't demand the child before the guard has spoken ("only comes forward after that part feels heard").
- PGQ-016 (source/PENDING-PUBLIC-GUIDE-CHANGES-2026-10-06-r2.md: "Memory support is not the same as reflective journaling"), queued for this practice (GUIDE-UPDATE-QUEUE-20261006.md): when reflective journaling makes experience more confusing, a short dated fact log, a what-helped note, a reminder, a next-step entry or a voice note keeps continuity without having to interpret at the same time; pattern-finding can come later if useful; a memory aid doesn't need to explain your life. Not in the r4 guide's text or the article yet: a second paragraph.
